Visited Kake Di Hatti, HSR Layout recently and had a good experience. The ambience is one of the best parts of this place — spacious seating, greenery, and a nice setup that gives proper North Indian restaurant vibes.

We tried Crispy Corn, Crispy Baby Corn, Chinese Bhel, Dahi Kebab, Paneer Tikka Masala, Garlic Naan, and Lassi. The Garlic Naan was the highlight for me, and the starters were quite tasty too. Portion sizes are generous, so it’s better to visit with family or friends and share dishes.

Service was quick and the staff were polite and attentive throughout the meal. The food reminded me of authentic North Indian flavors, especially the breads and main course.

The only thing I felt was that the pricing is on the higher side, which might be one reason the restaurant wasn’t very crowded during our visit. Apart from that, it’s a great place for vegetarians looking for good food and a pleasant dining experience in HSR.

We visited Kake Di Hatti with our family after hearing so much hype, but the experience was honestly very disappointing. The manager’s behavior was rude and lacked even basic hospitality or customer courtesy.

The biggest issue was the pricing versus quantity. Compared to restaurants like Meghana Foods, this place charges almost double for some dishes while serving barely one-third of the quantity. Around 8 of us ordered only starters and a few dishes, yet the bill crossed ₹3500 and nobody even felt properly satisfied.
The real surprise came afterward when we ate at Paratha Wala. The food there was delicious, fresh, filling, and reasonably priced. In comparison, Kake Di Hatti felt severely overpriced with poor value for money. Sadly, the reality was completely opposite of the hype.
Only zero star.

Highly recommended! I’d happily give them a 5/5.

Kake Di Hatti in HSR LAYOUT is a great spot if you're craving rich, flavorful North Indian vegetarian food. Their signature Haryali Butter Naan – Kake style is massive and delicious, perfectly paired with creamy, spicy gravies like the Dhuandar Paneer Butter Masala. The smoky and indulgent Dal Makhani is another must-try, slow-cooked to perfection with that signature buttery touch.

The ambiance is clean, spacious, and welcoming. It’s ideal for both casual dinners and family outings. Service is generally good, though it can be a bit slow during busy hours. Prices are on the higher side but the portions are generous, making it worth the spend.

Overall, Kake Di Hatti offers a satisfying and indulgent dining experience—just be ready for a bit of a wait during peak times!
